learning_outcomes.text: Students know the basic methods for describing and analyzing analog and digital systems, as well as the structure of basic circuits for analog and digital signal processing.
Students are able to understand and solve all tasks related to the analysis and interpretation of linear and time-invariant analog and time-discrete (digital) systems.

syllabus_topics: Basic concepts of signals and systems: Linearity and time-invariance: LTI systems, causality and stability.
Real/complex, symmetric, periodic, bounded and limited signals
Discontinuous and oscillatory elementary signals and their properties
Determination of transfer behavior using z-transformation
Transfer behavior in the time domain: Discrete convolution
Transfer function, impulse response, basic structures
Properties: Stability, eigenfunctions, IIR and FIR systems
The z-transformation, time-discrete and discrete Fourier-transformation
Determination of transfer behavior using Laplace transformation
Transfer behavior in the time domain: Continuous convolution
Transfer function, impulse response, basic structures
The Laplace and Fourier-Transformation, Fourier series
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded upon successful completion of the module exam.
